extracted.intended_audience: USPTO staff, policymakers, patent and trademark practitioners, applicants, and stakeholders interested in USPTO performance and program standards
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO patent and trademark performance metrics
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO performance-report guidance and metrics for evaluating and improving patent and trademark delivery, quality, timeliness, anti-fraud efforts, outreach, and related programs. Covers statutory compliance measures, pendency targets, quality assurance, technology adoption, workforce actions, and public-access initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Pro Bono Program matching
rubrics_metrics.description: The program’s network of regional programs matches volunteer patent professionals with financially underresourced inventors and small businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program performance measures include number of matched inventors (to date >4,200), volunteer hours logged (since 2015 ~110,000 hours), and assisted patent application filings (>2,100). The program also offers virtual and in-person “pathways” events to connect inventors with IP protection resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusion metrics for pro bono users
rubrics_metrics.description: Demographic measures of who uses the Patent Pro Bono Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveyed pro bono users reported 35% African American/Black, 14% Hispanic, 5.7% Asian American/Pacific Islander, 1.5% Native American; 43% identified as female and 7.9% as veteran. These metrics are used to assess outreach to traditionally underserved communities and program equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent timeliness goals based on PTA
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO establishes patent timeliness goals based on Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) compliance to statutory time frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reducing issued PTAs shortens pendency and increases applicant certainty. Strategies to meet PTA targets include catch-up overtime, revisions to examiner award programs, and increased hiring. Example: FY2023 mailed-actions PTA target 80% (achieved 81%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) Compliance, Mailed Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric measuring PTA compliance for mailed office actions (the agency’s adherence to statutorily defined time frames for actions the agency mails to applicants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess timeliness of USPTO-issued office actions; targets are set annually (e.g., FY2023 target 80%, actual 81%). Reducing issued PTAs provides shorter processing time for applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total PTA Compliance, Remaining Inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric measuring PTA compliance for remaining inventory (cases awaiting action from the agency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitors backlog-handling effectiveness; FY2023 target 86% vs actual 82%. Agency actions to improve include hiring and internal process adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent statutory compliance metrics — 35 U.S.C. 101 (utility/eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage metric that measures examiner compliance with 35 U.S.C. 101 requirements (utility and eligibility) in patent examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets are set (e.g., >94%) and tracked over reporting periods to ensure correctness of eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent statutory compliance metrics — 35 U.S.C. 102 (prior art compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage metric that measures examiner compliance with 35 U.S.C. 102 (novelty/prior art) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate correctness of prior-art-based rejections and prior art searching; targets typically set >94% or similar thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent statutory compliance metrics — 35 U.S.C. 103 (non-obviousness/prior art compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage metric that measures examiner compliance with 35 U.S.C. 103 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses quality of obviousness rejections and underlying prior art reasoning; targets and actual percentages are reported to indicate examination quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent statutory compliance metrics — 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description/claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage metric that measures examiner compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112 (including 112(a),(b) and 112(f)) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitors adequacy of written description, claim definiteness, and claim support decisions; used as part of the statutory compliance scorecard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality net promoter score from customer surveys on examination quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer-survey metric capturing perceptions of examiners’ adherence to rules and procedures and overall examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys invited >3,000 frequent customers; results reported as a quality net promoter score (e.g., 58) and percent rating work quality as good or excellent (>60%). Used to measure customer satisfaction and perceived correctness, clarity, and consistency of rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption and use of AI/ML tools by patent examiners (PE2E Search suite, Similarity Search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of examiner engagement with and usage of the Patents End-to-End (PE2E) Search suite and its AI features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracking includes percent of examiners using AI features (more than half), number of queries run (~1.5 million), and percent using Similarity Search (~67%). Agency emphasizes rigorous testing, examiner feedback, continuous improvements, and human oversight—AI is meant to empower examiners and improve prior art discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency technical testing and human oversight of AI tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation that technical teams perform rigorous testing on AI/ML tools and collect real-time examiner feedback, with human input central to model improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing assessments must meet performance standards and ensure AI suggests relevant information without replacing human judgment; continuous model improvement is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Dossier stewardship and access to IP5 work
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring patent examiners have access to the Global Dossier to view related IP5 agency work and prior art references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of IP5 work improves reliability of patentability determinations by exposing examiners to domestic and foreign cited references early in prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Program: random sampling of examiners' work products
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic review of a random sample of patent examiners’ work to assess examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides timely, reliable, and meaningful indicators of examination quality and serves as the foundation for assessing improvement efforts and reliability/consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investments in patent examination quality (application readiness, continuation practice, prior art and searching, training, prosecution changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives to improve patent durability and issuance of reliable, predictable patents through training and process changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes training on 35 U.S.C. 101/102/103/112 and search, stakeholder training on USPTO practices to improve applicant submissions, and programs to enhance examiner legal and technical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent examiner workforce management: special pay table, hiring, and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a special patent pay table and hiring targets to recruit and retain a technical STEM examination workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining competitive compensation (special rate requests per 5 CFR 530.304), hiring classes, and retention efforts are considered necessary to meet performance demands and reduce PTA/pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Average First Action Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time from filing to the examining attorney’s first office action for trademark applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitored as a top priority; example FY2023 first action pendency reported at 8.5 months (met planned target). Used to assess speed of initial examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Average Total Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time between filing and final disposition (abandonment, notice of allowance, or registration) for trademark applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backlogs can increase total pendency (FY2023 actual 14.6 months vs target 14.5). Reducing total pendency is an agency objective via hiring, process improvements, and automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark First Action Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage metric measuring compliance of first actions in trademark examination with rules and standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to monitor correctness of initial office actions; targets set annually (e.g., FY2023 target 95.5%, actual 96.8% exceeded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Final Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage metric measuring compliance of final dispositions in trademark examination with rules and standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitors quality of final decisions; targets set (e.g., FY2023 target 97.0%, actual 98.6% exceeded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark workforce initiatives (hiring examining attorneys/specialists, TMFlex paralegal support, exploring nonlawyer assistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staffing and role changes to improve trademark examination capacity and anti-scam efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include hiring examining attorneys (e.g., 86 in FY2023), adding specialists, establishing TMFlex to provide paralegal investigative support (streamlined anti-scam work and positively affected disposal pendency), and exploring nonlawyer roles to assist the application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark pendency transparency: website pendency widget
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing a pendency widget on Trademarks webpages showing the date of applications currently in examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented based on stakeholder feedback to increase transparency about examination timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark anti-scam efforts and Register Protection Office (RPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of the RPO and other measures to detect and combat fraudulent trademark filings and maintenance submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RPO staffed with examining attorneys, paralegals, and investigators; activities include publishing scam awareness webpages (auction sites, specimen farms), shutting down USPTO.gov accounts controlled by scammers, and moving suspicious files out of examination into administrative review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Modernization Act (TMA) implementation (shortened response times, identity verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of TMA phases to shorten response times and require identity verification for applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase two shortened preregistration office action response times from six months to three months (with potential extension to six months) to expedite examination and reduce scammers' ability to obstruct progress; identity verification introduced using ID.me for TEAS and TEAS International.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploring automation and process redesign (AI/ML/RPA/NLP) to improve Trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency initiatives to integrate AI, machine learning, robotic process automation, and natural language processing to improve capacity, efficiency, quality, and applicant experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party management consulting engagements, internal ideation sessions, and IT investments aim to optimize examination time, explore award incentives, streamline bad-faith processing, and reduce system downtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, outreach, and international capacity building (STOPfakes and road shows)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO programs to provide IP education, training, and capacity building domestically and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes STOPfakes.gov portal support, China IP Toolkit, China IP Road Shows, live STOPfakes road shows with partner agencies, and training for police, prosecutors, and customs officials to improve IP protection and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot programs to expedite examination for prioritized public-good technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot initiatives (e.g., Cancer Moonshot Expedited Examination, Climate Change Mitigation Pilot, Patents for Humanity) to accelerate examination for certain technologies addressing public goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs broaden qualifying technologies, offer expedited examination pathways, and include award competitions to incentivize innovations in areas like cancer immunotherapy, climate mitigation, and green energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Experience (CX) HISP designation and welcome letters
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO focus on customer experience for applying for a patent and registering a trademark as HISP-designated services and targeted communications to applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a High Impact Service Provider (per OMB Circular A-11, section 280), USPTO collects customer feedback and issues a HISP CX Action Plan; in FY2023 began sending “welcome letters” to patent and trademark applicants providing information on free trainings and resources to help applicants (notably pro se filers and underrepresented communities) navigate the IP ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions to address fraudulent patent filings and expedited/irregular filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency measures to detect and resolve irregular or fraudulent patent application filings that consume resources and delay legitimate applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include mailing applicants notices requesting information to resolve irregularities and awaiting statutory clarifications (e.g., authority under Unleashing American Innovators Act of 2022 to fine false entity status assertions). Efforts aim to reduce questionable filings that affect design application processing and revenue.
